_comment: Per-device preset overrides for lamp. See robots/contract/ROBOT-SPEC.md § Per-device presets. Lamp's LED ring is 32 pixels (vs the platform default of 64). All RGB channels in this overlay are capped at 3 for the low-glare device test; colors retain their hue as closely as integer channel values allow.
_comment_listening: Speed only; the color is the blue group value below. Base speed is 1.2, the fastest in EMOTION_PRESETS (every other breathing preset is 0.2-0.6), and it was reported as glaring on the lamp. Lowering the color had already been tried and did not help, because the level was never this cue's problem. breathing() sweeps 0 -> peak -> 0 over 100 steps of 0.03/speed, so modulation depth is 100% at every speed and only the period moves: 2.5 s at 1.2. A full-ring, full-depth swing that fast, sustained for as long as the user keeps talking, reads as pulsing rather than as light. 0.3 puts it back with the family. Confirmed by eye on lamp-0c89, 21/08/2026.
_comment_processing_group: The processing group (curious/thinking/scan/acknowledge) is dim purple-rose [3, 0, 2], hue 320 deg, NOT the green 120 deg slot the six-hue layout originally gave it. Green was reported as glaring on 25/08/2026 at [0, 4, 0], which is already the lowest the green tier goes: intensity 0.7 turns it into [0, 2, 0] on the strip, and one step lower is [0, 1, 0], where breathing/pulse truncate per frame and the cycle visibly steps. Level was therefore not the lever. The cause is the emitter, not the amplitude -- WS2812's green die is brighter than its red at the same value (the same finding that put the green tier at 4 while every other tier is 5), so EVERY green-dominant hue, 60 through 180 deg, carries the problem and no amount of dimming escapes it. Moving the group off green entirely is the only fix that keeps the whole ring lit. Green is held at exactly 0 for that reason -- this is about not waking the green die, not about keeping colors saturated, so red and blue may be mixed freely here. Red is reduced from 5 to 3 while blue remains at 2, lowering glare while keeping the color visibly purple.
_comment_status_led: All status LED RGB channels are capped at 3 for the low-glare device test. Effects and speeds remain inherited from the base presets. Verify that alert and privacy cues remain readable and that low-level breathing does not visibly step.
_comment_button_led: Button hold-warning RGB channels are capped at 3 for the low-glare device test. The driver distinguishes shutdown and factory reset through blink versus solid, not hue.
_comment_scene: Scene brightness only — hue (the color temperature mix) stays at the base value. Two things were wrong at the base levels. (1) reading/focus/energize all landed above lamp's max_brightness ceiling of 120, and clamp_color only scales DOWN, so all three collapsed to peak 120: three different scenes rendering as one, at the brightest level the ring can do. (2) Peak alone understates a scene: unlike an emotion cue, a scene lights all 32 pixels, so total flux is far higher than the peak number suggests — judging a scene by its peak the way we judge an indicator makes it come out too bright, which is what happened on the first pass here. Peaks now: energize 61, reading 48, focus 38, relax 25, movie 10, night 3. Night is deliberately far below the rest — it is a nightlight, meant to let you find your way without waking you, not to light the room; it is also blue-free by hue so it does not suppress melatonin. Spaced wider at the top because perceived brightness goes as roughly the cube root of value.
